title: Scripture and Restoration
definition: Scripture and Restoration means God uses His Word to bring sinners, sufferers, and wandering believers back toward truth, healing, obedience, and hope in Christ.
summary: Scripture and Restoration means God uses His Word to bring sinners, sufferers, and wandering believers back toward truth, healing, obedience, and hope in Christ.
christFocus: Jesus restores broken people by His grace, and Scripture reveals His mercy, correction, forgiveness, and renewing power.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Restoration in Scripture is not pretending sin and suffering never happened. It is God’s gracious work of bringing people back to Himself, renewing what is damaged, correcting what is wrong, and strengthening what is weak.

God’s Word restores by telling the truth. It exposes sin without denying grace. It comforts the broken without excusing rebellion. It calls the weary home without crushing them under shame.

Christ is the Restorer. He forgives sinners, heals the brokenhearted, restores failures, and sends the restored to serve. Scripture shows that a person’s story is not over when Christ is at work.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people believe they are too broken, too addicted, too disabled, too ashamed, or too wounded to be useful to God. Scripture and restoration directly confronts that lie with the mercy and power of Christ.

This doctrine also corrects shallow restoration that avoids repentance. Biblical restoration includes grace, truth, healing, accountability, and renewed obedience.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Bring your broken places honestly before God’s Word. Let Scripture correct what needs repentance, comfort what needs healing, and point you to Christ who restores by grace and empowers new obedience through the Holy Spirit.
